title: workflow-ledger command v1
description: One command against one stage run: `POST /v1/stage-runs/{stage_run_id}/commands`. Served by `schemas/workflow.py::CommandRequest`; the refusal vocabulary is `shepherd_workflow.state.RefusalClass` and the status mapping is `services/workflow_service.py`. An ACCEPTED command answers with the stage run shape published in `stage_run.v1.json#/properties/stage_run` -- the same object `GET /v1/stage-runs/{id}` returns, so a caller never reconciles two views of one row. That shape is not `$ref`-ed here on purpose: a cross-file reference that fails to resolve raises only when an instance is validated, so it would leave this file looking checked while checking nothing.

request.description: The shape is CLOSED. An unrecognised field is a 422 naming it, not silence: a client that misspells `state_version` would otherwise have its command applied at a version it never read, which is the concurrency guarantee removed by a typo.

kind.description: Every member of `CommandKind`, which is exactly the set that does NOT 422 as an unknown command. Being in this list is not a promise that the reducer accepts it against a given stage run: `start` against a pending stage run, for instance, reaches the lease check and is refused `lease_not_held`. A `kind` outside the list is a malformed request -- the engine never understood a command at all -- and is distinct from a refusal.

state_version.description: The version the caller READ. Not optional and not defaulted: a command that does not state the version it is acting on cannot be refused for acting on a stale one.

fence.description: The fence granted by the lease this caller holds. Required in practice for `complete` and `fail`, which are refused with `lease_not_held` or `stale_fence` without the current one. Null for `lease`, `cancel` and `expire`.

payload.description: Per-command fields the reducer reads: `payload_digest` and `provider_pin` on `complete`, `dispatch_key` on `lease`, `reason` on `fail`. Never `job_id`, `stage_key` or `workflow_digest` -- those come from the stored stage run, because a caller restating them can only ever restate them wrongly.

refusal.description: A refusal is an ANSWER: the engine understood the command and declined it. It is a 4xx naming the class, never a 5xx, because a caller that cannot tell a refusal from a failure cannot tell whether retrying is correct.

status.description: 404 when the stage run is not visible to this caller, which covers 'no such id' AND 'another org's id' -- see the tenancy row in contract.md. 409 when the ledger moved and re-reading then retrying is correct. 422 when retrying the command unchanged will not make it applicable.

detail.description: The refusal class VERBATIM. Match on this; it is the stable, machine-matchable half of the answer. The enum lists every member of `RefusalClass`, including ones no route in this slice has been shown to reach, so a class the package ADDS surfaces as a schema failure rather than as a silent new status code.
